notes: How this part was researched: one search per candidate, then the session's search allowance ran out (200 of 200) early in the second round, so follow-up searches for campaign sites, local party pages and news reports could not be made. Pages were then opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), robots.txt read first and obeyed. Filed campaign websites were learned from an existing scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) had been run; only race, name and the website cell were looked at. A second pass with searching would be worth it for the candidates with nothing below.

Not read, and nothing worked around: mncourts.gov (403 to scripts and to the page-reading tool, so no court page for Judge Erin Lindhart Felten or Judge Stoney L. Hiljus; search results say Felten was appointed by Governor Walz in 2024 and Hiljus by Governor Dayton in 2012, but no page stating it could be opened: mnbar.org refused the connection, and cfb.mn.gov's robots.txt asks scripts to stay out); co.ym.mn.gov (robots.txt; Yellow Medicine County sheriff); mankatomn.gov (robots.txt); kttc.com (robots.txt names ClaudeBot). mn.gov and the Secretary of State's sites were never asked.

Republican endorsements: none could be recorded for Jackie Henry (Senate 18) or Ben Bakeberg (Senate 54). mngop.com's '2026 Republican Nominees' page names neither, and no local unit's page was found without searching. A search result quoted the Mankato Free Press saying Henry's campaign has no website.

Left out on purpose. John Heinrich: the Legislative Reference Library marks his birth year 'uncertain', so no birth year. Bruce R. Anderson (Forest Lake mayor): search results return the late state senator Bruce D. Anderson, a different person; the city's council page shows Blake Roberts as mayor; nothing recorded. Don Friend (Mankato Ward 3): a search result says a Don Friend ran for the same ward in 2022 and lost narrowly, but the article could not be opened to tie him to this race. Pat "Pot" Farmer and Matthew Beukema: search results mention earlier school board runs (Rochester 2024, St. Francis 2024), which are not offices held. Jen Bloomquist's own About page mentions party posts in California; party posts are not public offices. Candidates' jobs are not recorded.

Nothing found for: Jackie Henry, Chad Ryan, Craig Smith, Michael Jenson, Kristy Kjos (Roseau County's site showed no page naming the county attorney), Bruce R. Anderson, David Sieburg, Duane Rader, Craig Johnson, Don Friend, Matthew Beukema, Chris Peach, Pat "Pot" Farmer, Zack Dinzeo (the district's own page lists him only as a candidate), Erin Lindhart Felten, Stoney L. Hiljus.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address was opened again (the page-reading tool, and the kit's downloader with its honest User-Agent where this machine's router dropped the lookup). Grant County, the City of Anoka and Prior Lake-Savage Area Schools have moved to new addresses (grantcountymn.gov, anokamn.gov, plsas.org); the old ones forward there, and the new ones are recorded. One finding removed (see 'removed').
